definition: The World Wide Web (WWW), often known as WWW, W3, or the Web, is the most widely used software platform on the globe. Tim Berners-Lee proposed the architecture of what became the World Wide Web. It is an information-based environment where users may access documents and other resources through the Internet using a web browser, allowing users to search for information by going from one page to the next. The Web has three constituent elements:  HTTP: Hypertext Transfer Protocol, managing the data exchange between the server and the client.  URL: Uniform Resource Locator, the address of a website on the Internet.  HTML: Hypertext Markup Language, the most common format for publishing web documents. A website consists of several web resources having a common topic and, in most cases, a shared domain name. A publisher can create website content, or it can be developed interactively from user-generated content.
